title: findgroups
summary: Assign sorted group numbers while preserving exact grouping identifiers.

gpu_support.notes: MATLAB does not document gpuArray support for findgroups. RunMat can gather resident grouping data only when the resident-input extension is enabled.

description: `G = findgroups(A)` assigns one-based double group numbers in sorted unique-key order. Numeric grouping includes all eight integer classes, whose values are compared exactly. Missing strings, empty character vectors, NaN, NaT, and undefined categorical values produce NaN in G.
behaviors: A must be a scalar or vector. G has the same size and row-or-column orientation as A.
`findgroups(A1,...,AN)` groups sorted unique tuples. Every input vector must have the same size, and a missing value in any role makes the corresponding G element NaN.
`[G,ID] = findgroups(A)` returns sorted unique identifiers in A's class. Integer IDs preserve authoritative values above flintmax.
`[G,ID1,...,IDN] = findgroups(A1,...,AN)` preserves each identifier output's corresponding input class.
`[G,TID] = findgroups(T)` groups all supported table variables and preserves their names and classes in TID.

Supported grouping variables are numeric, logical, string, cell arrays of character vectors, categorical, datetime, duration, and calendarDuration. Sparse and complex grouping variables reject explicitly.

Matrix-as-columns grouping, `findgroups(T,selector)`, timetable input, and resident input are independent gated RunMat extensions. The table selector form accepts exactly one selector and never ignores trailing arguments.

faqs.question: Are group numbers integer-typed?
faqs.answer: No. G contains positive integer-valued doubles and NaN for missing rows. Integer grouping identifiers retain their integer class in ID or TID.

faqs.question: Are integer values converted to double for grouping?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat compares authoritative signed or unsigned integer values directly, including values above flintmax.

faqs.question: Can I pass a matrix as A?
faqs.answer: MATLAB documents grouping vectors. RunMat can interpret matrix columns as grouping roles only when the matrix-as-columns extension is enabled.

faqs.question: Can findgroups consume GPU-resident data?
faqs.answer: Only in RunMat extension mode. The gate is checked recursively before any resident input or table variable is gathered.

faqs.question: Does findgroups accept timetables?
faqs.answer: Timetable input is a separate RunMat extension. Its identifier output is currently an ordinary table of selected variable values; row times are not grouping variables.
